page_title: WhatCable: Know what your USB-C cable can really do

summary.name: WhatCable
summary.one_liner: WhatCable is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app (with a CLI) that reads USB-C cable, charger, and device data on Apple Silicon Macs and explains in plain English what is limiting charging or display speed.
keywords: why is my mac charging slowly
use_cases: Diagnose why a MacBook charges slowly
Check whether a USB-C cable supports the speed or wattage it claims
Find out if the cable, charger, or Mac port is the bottleneck
Confirm a monitor is getting full resolution and refresh rate over USB-C or Thunderbolt
Scripted USB-C cable diagnostics via JSON output
summary.what_it_does: WhatCable reads the USB-C and USB Power Delivery details macOS exposes, including the cable's e-marker identity, speed, and current rating. It shows what the charger offers and whether the Mac is drawing the power it needs, and gives a plain-English verdict on whether the Mac port, cable, or device is limiting the link. For connected monitors it checks whether full resolution and refresh are reached. A cable trust section flags e-marker fields that look inconsistent with USB PD rules, and a bundled CLI offers text, JSON, and watch modes.
notable: Free and open source under MIT licence, with no ads or tracking; optional Pro adds cable history and live power metering
Plain-English verdicts on whether cable, charger, or Mac is limiting charging speed
Cable trust checks compare e-marker data against USB-IF vendor list and PD spec ranges
Available in 19 languages and includes a CLI with JSON and watch mode
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later; the page says Intel Macs do not expose the needed USB-PD data
Pro is a one-time £9.99 purchase for up to two Macs; advanced features like live metering and cable history are Pro-only
Cannot inspect physical cable wiring; a missing or unusual e-marker does not prove a cable is counterfeit
